name: Ho Chi Minh City Museum
overview: A place that preserves the story of Saigon across many centuries
history: This building was once a colonial-era governor's residence. It later became a museum holding thousands of artifacts about the city's history, culture, and development.
greenStoryHook: This area gets crowded with vehicles. Parking at the April 30th Park lot and walking in helps you appreciate the architecture at a slower pace while easing pressure on the heritage zone.
walkingRoute: April 30th Park (400m away) → walk along Ly Tu Trong Street → Museum
ecoBenefit: Reduce 120-150kg of CO2 per day in the area and protect the heritage landscape
hiddenSpot: The museum garden behind the building has a quiet pocket in the middle of the city

name: September 23rd Park
overview: A community gathering space and a center for charity and cultural activity
history: The park was built to serve public recreation needs and became a long-standing meeting place for Saigon residents.
greenStoryHook: This place gets very crowded, especially during peak hours. Park in the outer lot or use the main park lot. Do not squeeze into the park itself; it creates traffic and affects the leisure area.
walkingRoute: Main park lot → walk 3-5 minutes into the park core
ecoBenefit: Reduce traffic, add green space, and support lower air pollution
hiddenSpot: A quiet corner in the north side of the park, with few foreign visitors

name: 127 Nguyen Trai Alley (Bun Moc Co Sau)
overview: A famous local eatery and a strong example of Saigon's real food culture
history: Opened in the 1980s, this shop grew from a small kitchen at the back of the alley into a local food legend. Aunt Sau still cooks the broth in the traditional way.
greenStoryHook: The alley is too narrow for large parking. Park in the alley lot, then explore slowly to notice the other eateries and lesser-known corners. It is calmer and feels more authentic.
walkingRoute: Nguyen Trai parking lot (150m away) → walk into Alley 127 → Aunt Sau's shop
ecoBenefit: Reduce pressure on narrow-alley traffic and encourage pedestrian-friendly community exploration
recommendedParking: Small lot on Nguyen Trai or a nearby alley
hiddenSpot: Breakfast stalls and fresh produce vendors deeper in the alley, opening as early as 5-6 a.m.
